ai.title: Base2 agent prompt: forbid spawning context-pruner
ai.summary: Added explicit instruction to base2 agent prompt in .agents/base2/base2.ts to never spawn the context-pruner agent. Prevents redundant agent spawning since context pruning runs automatically. Internal prompt constraint only.

eli5.text: The automated assistant has been given a clear instruction not to manually start the background cleanup tool, because that tool already turns on by itself. This is a behind-the-scenes tweak to the assistant's internal guidance, so there's nothing new you would see or need to do; it just keeps the system from doing the same cleanup task twice by accident.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.557 ships error cleanup and clickable usage banner
ai.summary: Freebuff 1.0.557 consolidates error utilities by routing CLI error handling through `getErrorObject` from `@codebuff/common/util/error` and dropping `cli/src/utils/error.ts`, while the agent runtime trims verbose `APICallError` output to just the error message. The usage banner text is now a clickable button that opens `WEBSITE_URL + '/usage'` via `open()`, backed by `cli/src/components/bottom-banner.tsx`, `cli/src/components/usage-banner.tsx`, and `cli/src/utils/usage-banner-state.ts`. The base2 agent prompt in `.agents/base2/base2.ts` now forbids spawning the context-pruner agent, since pruning runs automatically.
ai.evidence: Diff shows `cli/release/package.json` version field changed from 1.0.556 to 1.0.557. Release notes for 1.0.557 include error utility consolidation, clickable CLI usage banner, and base2 agent prompt context-pruner spawn prevention.

eli5.text: Freebuff 1.0.557 makes error messages easier to read and adds a clickable button to view usage details. When the tool encounters a problem with an external service, it now shows a simpler, cleaner explanation instead of dumping technical details like URLs and headers, while still keeping the full information available behind the scenes. The usage banner at the bottom of the screen now includes a 'See more' link you can click to open a page about your usage directly in your web browser. A small update to the agent prompt also prevents unnecessary agent processes from being spawned, which helps keep things running smoothly. Upgrading gives you cleaner error reporting, quicker access to usage info, and a more efficient experience overall.

ai.title: Add AI SDK schema validation to convertCbToModelMessages
ai.summary: Added strict validation of aggregated messages against `modelMessageSchema` from the `ai` package in `convertCbToModelMessages`. This change introduces a loop that calls `safeParse` on each message, throwing a descriptive error if validation fails, and optionally logs the failure details via a new `logger` parameter. The update affects `common/src/util/messages.ts`, ensuring malformed message structures are caught early before reaching the provider.

eli5.text: When the system prepares messages to send to an AI model, it now checks each message against an expected format before sending it. If any message is missing required pieces, the system stops and reports exactly which message caused the problem. This helps catch broken or incomplete messages early, before they reach the AI model. This check is live today.

ai.title: Restrict spawnable agents when agentId provided
ai.summary: The agent runtime now conditionally merges available agents into spawnable subagents. If an `agentId` is present, the system strictly uses `mainAgentTemplate.spawnableAgents`, bypassing the union with `availableAgents`. This prevents unintended agent spawning when a specific agent is targeted. The change applies to `packages/agent-runtime/src/main-prompt.ts`.

eli5.text: When you tell the assistant exactly which specialist to talk to, it now sticks to that specialist and won't pull in the full list of available helpers. If you don't name a specific specialist, it still combines the default helpers with any extra ones that are available. This means targeting one specialist keeps the conversation focused instead of letting the assistant reach for unrelated helpers.

ai.title: main-prompt test fix
ai.summary: Updated `main-prompt.test.ts` to assert that `spawnableAgents` excludes other local agents when a specific `agentId` is provided. The test now verifies that `spawnableAgents` remains empty unless explicitly defined in the agent's template, preventing auto-addition of all available agents.

eli5.text: The assistant no longer assumes other local agents are available just because one is selected. When you target a specific agent by name, it will only use the agents that were explicitly listed in that agent's own configuration, rather than pulling in every agent the system knows about. The automated checks that verify this behavior have been corrected to enforce this rule, so the system now matches the intended design.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.558 ships schema validation and spawnable agent gating
ai.summary: Freebuff 1.0.558 rolls up two minor updates into a single release. Message validation in `convertCbToModelMessages` (common/src/util/messages.ts) now runs each aggregated message through `modelMessageSchema` from the `ai` package, throwing a descriptive error on failure and optionally logging details via a new `logger` parameter, so malformed structures are caught before reaching the provider. The agent runtime in `packages/agent-runtime/src/main-prompt.ts` now strictly uses `mainAgentTemplate.spawnableAgents` when an `agentId` is supplied, bypassing the union with `availableAgents` to prevent unintended subagent spawning. These changes are reflected in the updated `cli/release/package.json` version field.
ai.evidence: Version field bumped from 1.0.557 to 1.0.558 in cli/release/package.json; release updates include AI SDK schema validation in convertCbToModelMessages and restricted spawnable agents when agentId is provided.

eli5.text: Freebuff 1.0.558 improves reliability and control for users working with multiple AI agents. The update adds strict validation that checks message formats before they are sent to AI providers, catching malformed data early so conversations stay consistent and errors are easier to diagnose. It also tightens control over which helper agents can be launched: when you specify a particular agent, only that agent can spawn its designated sub-agents, preventing unexpected agents from starting up. Finally, new tests confirm this behavior, ensuring that agent selection works predictably. Upgrading gives you better message reliability, clearer error reporting, and more precise control over automated agent workflows.
